Lecture 12

Homogeneous spaces and compact induction

Let KKK be a compact Lie group and HHH a closed subgroup. Which irreducible representations of KKK occur in functions on K/HK/HK/H, and how often? We show that each irreducible representation VVV of KKK occurs dim⁡VH\dim V^HdimVH times. Induction from HHH extends this count to vector-valued functions.

By the end of this lecture you will be able to:

  • Construct the invariant integral on K/HK/HK/H and identify L2(K/H)L^2(K/H)L2(K/H) with the right-HHH-invariant part of L2(K)L^2(K)L2(K).
  • Prove that each irreducible VVV occurs in L2(K/H)L^2(K/H)L2(K/H) exactly dim⁡VH\dim V^HdimVH times.
  • Define compact induction, describe an element of the induced representation in the tangent-field model on S2S^2S2, and prove Frobenius reciprocity with finite multiplicities.
  • Decompose L2(S2)L^2(S^2)L2(S2) under SO⁡(3)\SO(3)SO(3) and relate the summands to spherical harmonics.

Throughout, KKK is a compact Lie group, not necessarily connected, and H⊆KH\subseteq KH⊆K is a closed subgroup. By Lecture 3, K/HK/HK/H is a compact manifold, and the projection p ⁣:K→K/Hp\colon K\to K/Hp:K→K/H, p(x)=xHp(x)=xHp(x)=xH, is continuous and open. The group KKK acts on K/HK/HK/H by g⋅xH=gxHg\cdot xH=gxHg⋅xH=gxH.

The Haar measures dxdxdx on KKK and dhdhdh on HHH have total mass 111. They are left, right and inversion invariant (Lecture 5). The space L2(K)L^2(K)L2(K) is the completion of C(K)C(K)C(K) for ⟨f1,f2⟩=∫Kf1‾ f2 dx\langle f_1,f_2\rangle=\int_K\overline{f_1}\,f_2\,dx⟨f1​,f2​⟩=∫K​f1​​f2​dx, and C(K)→L2(K)C(K)\to L^2(K)C(K)→L2(K) is injective (Lecture 10).

We use the left and right translation representations (Lgf)(x)=f(g−1x),(Rgf)(x)=f(xg).(L_gf)(x)=f(g^{-1}x),\qquad(R_gf)(x)=f(xg).(Lg​f)(x)=f(g−1x),(Rg​f)(x)=f(xg). These commuting representations are unitary and strongly continuous (Lecture 10).

12.1 Functions and integration on K/HK/HK/H

By the definition of the quotient topology, a function φ\varphiφ on K/HK/HK/H is continuous exactly when φ∘p\varphi\circ pφ∘p is continuous. A right-HHH-invariant function on KKK is constant on cosets. Hence the pullback p∗p^*p∗ is a linear bijection p∗ ⁣:C(K/H)→C(K)H:={f∈C(K):f(xh)=f(x) for all x∈K, h∈H},p∗φ=φ∘p.\begin{equation} \label{lec12:eq:pullback} p^*\colon C(K/H)\to C(K)^H:=\{f\in C(K): f(xh)=f(x)\ \text{for all } x\in K,\ h\in H\},\qquad p^*\varphi=\varphi\circ p. \end{equation}p∗:C(K/H)→C(K)H:={f∈C(K):f(xh)=f(x) for all x∈K, h∈H},p∗φ=φ∘p.(12.1)

(b) The map (x,h)↦f(xh)(x,h)\mapsto f(xh)(x,h)↦f(xh) is uniformly continuous on the compact space K×HK\times HK×H. So fHf^HfH is continuous. For k∈Hk\in Hk∈H, left invariance of dhdhdh gives fH(xk)=∫Hf(xkh) dh=fH(x)f^H(xk)=\int_Hf(xkh)\,dh=f^H(x)fH(xk)=∫H​f(xkh)dh=fH(x). Fubini for continuous functions on K×HK\times HK×H and right invariance of dxdxdx give ∫KfH(x) dx=∫H∫Kf(xh) dx dh=∫H∫Kf(x) dx dh=∫Kf(x) dx.\int_Kf^H(x)\,dx=\int_H\int_Kf(xh)\,dx\,dh=\int_H\int_Kf(x)\,dx\,dh=\int_Kf(x)\,dx.∫K​fH(x)dx=∫H​∫K​f(xh)dxdh=∫H​∫K​f(x)dxdh=∫K​f(x)dx. A positive normalised invariant integral III on K/HK/HK/H is unique. Indeed, the map g↦φ(g−1 ⋅ )g\mapsto\varphi(g^{-1}\,\cdot\,)g↦φ(g−1⋅) is continuous in the supremum norm. So averaging the identity I(φ)=I(φ(g−1 ⋅ ))I(\varphi)=I(\varphi(g^{-1}\,\cdot\,))I(φ)=I(φ(g−1⋅)) over KKK gives I(φ)=I(∫Kφ(g−1 ⋅ ) dg)I(\varphi)=I\bigl(\int_K\varphi(g^{-1}\,\cdot\,)\,dg\bigr)I(φ)=I(∫K​φ(g−1⋅)dg). In particular, for a maximal torus H=TH=TH=T of a compact connected group KKK, this integral is the measure d(gT)d(gT)d(gT) of Lecture 9.

Definition 12.3. The space L2(K/H)L^2(K/H)L2(K/H) is the completion of C(K/H)C(K/H)C(K/H) for ⟨φ,ψ⟩=∫K/Hφ‾ ψ dξ\langle\varphi,\psi\rangle=\int_{K/H}\overline{\varphi}\,\psi\,d\xi⟨φ,ψ⟩=∫K/H​φ​ψdξ. The operator of the next proposition replaces a function by its average over each coset. Averaging does not increase an L2L^2L2 norm, and it does not change a function that is constant on cosets. So it is the projector onto invariants of Lecture 5, on an infinite-dimensional space.

The same weight basis counts tangent fields. In the tangent model, τ\tauτ has the weights 111 and −1-1−1. 12.5 Self-checks

  1. Let KKK be a finite group, regarded as a compact Lie group of dimension zero, and let H≤KH\le KH≤K be a subgroup. What does the multiplicity theorem (Theorem 12.7) say?

    Answer. Here L2(K/H)=C[K/H]L^2(K/H)=\C[K/H]L2(K/H)=C[K/H] is the permutation representation. An irreducible VVV occurs dim⁡VH\dim V^HdimVH times. This is finite-group Frobenius reciprocity for the trivial character of HHH.

  2. Why not define Φ(T)v=(Tv)(e)\Phi(T)v=(Tv)(e)Φ(T)v=(Tv)(e) directly for T ⁣:Vσ→L2-Ind⁡HKWT\colon V_\sigma\to L^2\text{-}\operatorname{Ind}_H^KWT:Vσ​→L2-IndHK​W?

    Answer. An L2L^2L2 class has no value at eee. Lemma 12.6 on equivariant images first shows that TTT takes continuous values.

  3. What are the multiplicities for H={e}H=\{e\}H={e} and for H=KH=KH=K?

    Answer. For H={e}H=\{e\}H={e}, σ\sigmaσ occurs dσd_\sigmadσ​ times in L2(K)L^2(K)L2(K). For H=KH=KH=K, a nontrivial irreducible has VK=0V^K=0VK=0, so only the trivial representation occurs, once, as the constants.

Summary

The invariant integral on K/HK/HK/H is the Haar integral of pullbacks. The averaging operator AHA_HAH​ projects L2(K)L^2(K)L2(K) onto L2(K)H≅L2(K/H)L^2(K)^H\cong L^2(K/H)L2(K)H≅L2(K/H). Peter–Weyl then shows that each σ∈Irr⁡(K)\sigma\in\Irr(K)σ∈Irr(K) occurs in L2(K/H)L^2(K/H)L2(K/H) exactly dim⁡VσH\dim V_\sigma^HdimVσH​ times.

Let VVV be a finite-dimensional representation of KKK and WWW a finite-dimensional unitary representation of HHH. An element of Ind⁡HKW\operatorname{Ind}_H^KWIndHK​W is a function on KKK fixed on each coset by its value at one point, and on S2S^2S2 with W=C2W=\C^2W=C2 it is a tangent field with complex components, written in moving frames. Evaluation at eee gives Hom⁡K(V,Ind⁡HKW)≅Hom⁡H(V∣H,W)\Hom_K(V,\operatorname{Ind}_H^KW)\cong\Hom_H(V|_H,W)HomK​(V,IndHK​W)≅HomH​(V∣H​,W). Isotypic vectors in L2-Ind⁡HKWL^2\text{-}\operatorname{Ind}_H^KWL2-IndHK​W are continuous. So σ\sigmaσ occurs in L2-Ind⁡HKWL^2\text{-}\operatorname{Ind}_H^KWL2-IndHK​W exactly dim⁡Hom⁡H(Vσ∣H,W)\dim\Hom_H(V_\sigma|_H,W)dimHomH​(Vσ​∣H​,W) times.

On S2=SO⁡(3)/SO⁡(2)S^2=\SO(3)/\SO(2)S2=SO(3)/SO(2) each SO⁡(3)\SO(3)SO(3)-module VℓV_\ellVℓ​ occurs once in L2(S2)L^2(S^2)L2(S2), realised by spherical harmonics of degree ℓ\ellℓ.
